engines.creator: Mara Quill
steps: compress the method to three steps
engines.strength: Speed and evidence density. Nothing is asserted that is not also shown.
engines.risk_if_copied_wholesale: Copied straight, this makes you a tool-tip account with no worldview. It never establishes that YOU have built anything - it only establishes that the technique works. An account of nothing but tips is replaceable by the next account with the same tips.

engines.creator: Theo Bright
engines.strength: Owned intellectual property and genuine teaching authority.
engines.risk_if_copied_wholesale: The length and the certainty are only earned by having actually built the thing for years. Adopting the framework-naming voice before you have the results behind it reads as a guru performance, and viewers detect it faster than you expect.

shared_grammar: The spoken line determines the visual - important nouns and claims get literal visual counterparts.
One primary idea per composition; the frame always has an obvious focal point.
Returning to the creator's face works as punctuation, marking sections rather than delivering information.
Proof appears next to the claim it supports, not collected at the end.
Captions are rhythm, and coexist with headings, labels and source text as separate systems.
Transitions are editorially motivated - hard cuts and mode changes, not generic wipes.
The hook is visually legible before the first sentence finishes.
The CTA is quieter than the body and asks for exactly one thing.

differences.what_i_take: Let the idea choose the length. A technique is short; a system that must be understood is long. Forcing one template onto both is why my early videos felt padded.
Fast for proof sequences, slow for anything requiring comprehension. These are two different speeds for two different jobs, not one average.
Both. My own finished pieces as external proof, plus a named way of thinking that is mine.
Hands during work, face for judgment calls and anything the viewer has to take my word for.

visual_modes.use_for: Hook, personal judgment, conviction, section reset, CTA

visual_modes.composition: Overhead or close bench shot, hands in frame, no face
visual_modes.use_for: Any physical technique as it actually happens
visual_modes.avoid_for: Anything abstract, or a claim about outcomes

visual_modes.composition: Fullscreen result, comparison, or measurement with legible numbers
visual_modes.use_for: Named evidence, before/after, a claimed result

visual_modes.composition: Persistent diagram where parts accumulate in narration order
visual_modes.avoid_for: A single fact with no relationships in it

visual_modes.composition: One phrase or number, restrained animation
visual_modes.use_for: A reveal, a contrast, a section title, the payoff
visual_modes.avoid_for: Ordinary spoken captions or filler words

mode_selection_rules.spoken_beat: An exact number or result is claimed

pacing_targets.face_reset_rule: After a dense proof sequence, at any section change, and before a personal conclusion.

typography_hierarchy: Speech captions - short spoken chunks, bold sans, placed against the active composition
Emphasis captions - one operative word gets color, weight or scale
Scene headline - names the current concept, stays long enough to orient
Diagram labels - compact, attached spatially to the object
Editorial impact text - two to six words, composition scale, reveals only
Source text - preserved from the real artifact, or recreated faithfully for legibility
motion_hierarchy: Hard cut or punch-in for a change in argument
Mode switch for a change in information type
Progressive reveal for a process or relationship
Highlight or trace on the exact object being discussed
Micro-motion for polish, only after comprehension is already solved
anti_patterns: Carousels of floating panels that relate to nothing being said
Motion that begins before the narration has given the viewer a reason to watch it
Flashing a screenshot too briefly to read - zoom and hold instead
Collapsing every text role into one caption component
Illustrating symbolically when the real action could honestly be shown
A CTA promising a resource that does not exist yet

synthesis.positioning_statement: Someone who actually builds furniture, showing the specific techniques, failures and judgment calls that make the work faster - with the finished piece always on camera as the proof.

script_formula: Specific hook - lead with the technique or the contrarian truth, never with biography
Fast credibility proof - the finished piece, on camera, supporting the promise
Personal reset - one line establishing why I am the one saying this
The useful process - taught with real work, in the order someone would do it
Boundary - what this does NOT mean, so the claim stays credible
Payoff - what is now faster, cheaper or less likely to fail
Positioning CTA - one aligned ask, and only if the resource actually exists
